mainTopic: Partitions and ladders between a מרפסת and a חצר, the שיור left out of a city's עירוב, and a new משנה on placing a עירוב for walking on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a מרפסת and a חצר that did not make an עירוב. The גמרא deflects it by explaining that the case is a low מרפסת, fenced except for an opening of up to ten אמות, which a small partition cuts off. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that a wall lined with ladders still counts as a מחיצה. רב ברונא challenges this from another statement of שמואל, and the same answer resolves it. Next comes the story of אביי making an עירוב for קקונאי, where he goes back and forth on whether the שיור (the section left out of a city's עירוב) must be a place that could have joined. He finally learns from פומבדיתא that it need not. The גמרא then explains the משנה's measure 'like חדשה', the views of רבי שמעון and רבי יצחק on the size of the שיור, and אביי's lesson that learning is not just a song. Finally a new משנה begins about a person whose house and עירוב lie in opposite directions, and about where an עירוב may be placed. That last case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רב נחמן's balcony ruling (in שמואל's name) used as a challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's statement in the name of שמואל ends: if the people of the מרפסת and the חצר did not make an עירוב, a partition of four טפחים in front of the מרפסת stops it from restricting the חצר. Without that partition, the מרפסת restricts the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and they did not make an עירוב: if there is a partition four טפחים wide in front of them, the מרפסת does not restrict the חצר. If there is no partition, it does restrict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל about a מרפסת connected to a חצר. It brings this as a challenge to רב נחמן's own earlier ruling (ומי אמר רב נחמן הכי?).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real partition (דקה) separates the מרפסת from the חצר. Without one, the connection through the ladder makes the two areas restrict each other, even though this leads to a stricter result. That seems to prove that a ladder always counts as an entrance, which challenges רב נחמן's earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: they made an עירוב, joining domains so that carrying is allowed
a balcony or upper gallery that people reach from the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a statement of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל. The case itself (a מרפסת above a חצר reached by a ladder) was introduced on the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: and they did not make an eiruv,
phrases.notes: The residents of the balcony and the courtyard forgot to join together.

phrases.english: if there is a partition of four [handbreadths] in front of them,
it does not prohibit [the courtyard],
and if not, it prohibits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ לִפְנֵיהֶם דַּקָּה אַרְבָּעָה אֵינָהּ אוֹסֶרֶת וְאִם לָאו אוֹסֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement of רב נחמן (in שמואל's name) that was introduced on the previous amud as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier position about how a ladder between two areas is treated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the ladder connection as an open entrance even when that makes things stricter. Only a partition of four טפחים removes that status.

steps.title: The balcony is less than ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this statement is about a מרפסת that is not ten טפחים high, so it is part of the חצר and proves nothing about ladders.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the מרפסת is not ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge by limiting the statement to a low מרפסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מרפסת lower than ten טפחים is not its own domain. It is basically part of the חצר, so the ladder plays no role at all. The ruling therefore teaches nothing about whether a ladder counts as an entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: with what case are we dealing here? (a formula that limits a source to a specific case)
ten (here, ten טפחים, the height that makes a separate domain)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where the balcony is not ten [handbreadths] high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to prove that a ladder always makes an entrance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a low מרפסת that is already part of the חצר, so it says nothing about ladders.

steps.title: Then why would a partition help?
steps.stepSummary: If the מרפסת is part of the חצר, adding a small partition should not change anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the מרפסת is not ten טפחים high, what difference does it make when one puts up a partition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. It sets up the need to define the case more precisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A low מרפסת is already merged with the חצר. A four-טפחים partition should not be enough to separate it, yet the ברייתא says it does. So the answer as given does not fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: what of it? what difference does it make?

phrases.english: But if the balcony is not ten high,
when he makes a partition,
what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limitation to a מרפסת lower than ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מרפסת is part of the חצר, a small partition should not separate it, yet the ברייתא says it does.

steps.title: A balcony fenced except for an opening of up to ten אמות
steps.stepSummary: The מרפסת is fenced off all around except for an opening of up to ten אמות. Putting a partition in that opening cuts it off from the חצר completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a מרפסת that is fenced off, leaving an opening of up to ten אמות. Since he puts up a partition there, he removes himself completely from the חצר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a further detail to the case, which explains why the partition works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fence already separates the מרפסת from the חצר. Only the opening, up to ten אמות wide, still connects them. A partition placed in that opening closes the last link, so the מרפסת is no longer part of the חצר.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove that a ladder always makes an entrance. It is about a low מרפסת, fenced except for an opening of up to ten אמות, which a partition cuts off from the חצר.

phrases.english: With [a balcony] fenced off, [leaving an opening] up to ten cubits,
for since he makes a partition,
he has completely removed himself from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by defining the case more precisely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A low מרפסת is fully merged with the חצר, so a partition should not help.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מרפסת is fenced except for an opening of up to ten אמות, so a partition in that opening separates it.

steps.title: A wall lined with ladders is still a partition
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that a wall lined with ladders, even along more than ten אמות, keeps the status of a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a wall that one lined with ladders, even along more than ten אמות, still has the status of a מחיצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of שמואל about ladders set against a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a gap of more than ten אמות ruins a wall's status as a מחיצה. Ladders do not create such a gap. The wall is still standing behind them, so it remains a valid partition.

keyTerms.meaning: he lined it, covering it all along
the legal status of a partition

steps.whyThisMatters: Ladders may give people a way to go up and over a wall, but they do not cancel the wall as a מחיצה, no matter how long the stretch they cover.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A wall that one lined with ladders,
even along more than ten [cubits],
it has the status of a partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ruling about ladders set against a wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ladders lining a wall, even along more than ten אמות, do not cancel its status as a מחיצה.

steps.title: רב ברונא challenges שמואל's ladder ruling from another statement of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב ברונא asks: how can שמואל say a ladder-lined wall is still a מחיצה, when רב נחמן quotes שמואל saying that a מרפסת without a partition restricts the חצר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ברונא raised a contradiction to רב יהודה in the winepress of רב חנינא's house. Did שמואל really say the wall keeps the status of a partition? But רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: if the people of a מרפסת and the people of a חצר forgot and did not make an עירוב, then if there is a partition of four in front of it, it does not restrict. If not, it restricts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל from step 5. It uses another statement that רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same statement about the מרפסת that the גמרא already raised in step 1. There it was set against רב נחמן; here רב ברונא sets it against רב יהודה's report of שמואל, which turns it into a contradiction inside שמואל himself. The ladders going up to the מרפסת seem to connect it to the חצר, so the wall would not separate them. That clashes with saying the wall stays a מחיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He threw at him, meaning he raised a contradiction between two sources
Winepress (the place where this discussion took place)
The legal status of a partition
Who forgot and did not make an עירוב together

steps.confusionAlert: This looks like a repeat of steps 1 to 4, and it mostly is. The difference is the target: in step 1 the statement was set against רב נחמן's own ruling, and here it is set against רב יהודה's report of שמואל, so the question is whether שמואל contradicts himself.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב בְּרוֹנָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rav Beruna raised a contradiction to Rav Yehuda
in the winepress of Rav Chanina's house:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל תּוֹרַת מְחִיצָה עָלָיו?
phrases.english: Did Shmuel really say it has the status of a partition?
But didn't Rav Nachman say in the name of Shmuel:
the people of a balcony and the people of a courtyard
who forgot and did not make an eiruv,
if there is a partition of four in front of it
phrases.notes: Four טפחים, placed in front of the balcony's entrance

phrases.english: it does not restrict,
and if not, it restricts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב בְּרוֹנָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the מימרא of step 5 using another statement of the same אמורא
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a ladder-lined wall keeps the status of a מחיצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere treats a מרפסת with ladders as connected to the חצר unless a partition is added. That suggests ladders cancel separation, which contradicts his ruling here.

steps.title: The balcony is less than ten handbreadths high
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שמואל's case is a מרפסת lower than ten טפחים, which counts as part of the חצר anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? One where the מרפסת is not ten high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. It says שמואל's מרפסת case is about a low מרפסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מרפסת lower than ten טפחים is part of the חצר whether or not there are ladders. So the ladders play no role in that case, and there is no contradiction with the ladder ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here (introduces a narrowing of the case)
Ten טפחים high, the height needed to count as a separate area

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
Where the balcony is not ten high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 6 the same way step 2 answered step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's מרפסת was thought to be connected to the חצר because of the ladders
steps.terutzMaskana: The מרפסת is connected because it is lower than ten טפחים, not because of the ladders

steps.title: Then why would a small partition help?
steps.stepSummary: If the low מרפסת is part of the חצר, a four-טפח partition should not separate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the מרפסת is not ten high, what difference does it make when he puts up a partition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A low מרפסת is part of the חצר. A small four-טפח board should not change that, so שמואל's rule that the partition helps seems to make no sense.

phrases.english: And if the balcony is not ten high,
when he puts up a partition, what difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל's case is a low מרפסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מרפסת is already part of the חצר, a small partition should not cut it off, yet שמואל says the partition helps

steps.title: The balcony is fenced except for an opening of up to ten cubits
steps.stepSummary: The מרפסת is walled in all around except for an opening of up to ten אמות. A partition in that opening fully separates it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where it is fenced in, with an opening of up to ten אמות. Since he puts up a partition, it is completely removed from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly what kind of low מרפסת שמואל meant, so that the partition does make a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the מרפסת is already walled off. Its only link to the חצר is the opening, which counts as a doorway because it is ten אמות or less. A partition placed there closes that doorway, so the מרפסת no longer belongs to the חצר. The ladder ruling of שמואל therefore stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Fenced in or enclosed all around
Up to ten אמות, the largest width that still counts as an opening (doorway)
It is completely removed (from the חצר)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's two statements do not clash. The מרפסת ruling is about a low, enclosed מרפסת whose opening gets closed by a partition. It has nothing to do with ladders, so a ladder-lined wall stays a מחיצה.

phrases.english: Where it is fenced in, with an opening of up to ten cubits,
for since he puts up a partition,
it is completely removed from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 and closes the challenge against שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A small partition seemed meaningless for a מרפסת that is part of the חצר
steps.terutzMaskana: The partition closes the only opening of an enclosed מרפסת, so it separates it from the חצר completely

steps.title: The people of קקונאי ask רב יוסף for someone to make their עירוב
steps.stepSummary: People from קקונאי ask רב יוסף for someone to make an עירוב for their city. רב יוסף sends אביי and tells him to make it beyond criticism.
steps.simpleTranslation: Certain people of קקונאי came before רב יוסף. They said to him: Give us a man who will make an עירוב for our city. He said to אביי: Go make an עירוב for them, and make sure there is no outcry against it in the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about making an עירוב for a whole city. This step sets the scene for אביי's decisions in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קקונאי was a city that had once belonged to the public and later became private. The משנה rules that such a city may not be included in the עירוב in full. Some section must be left out (a שיור), so the עירוב needed expert care. רב יוסף warns אביי to make it so solid that no one in the בית מדרש could object.

keyTerms.meaning: The בית מדרש, the study hall

phrases.english: Certain people of Kakunya
who came before Rav Yosef,
said to him: Give us a man
who will make an eiruv for our city.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְאַבָּיֵי: זִיל עָרֵב לְהוּ,
phrases.english: He said to Abaye: Go make an eiruv for them,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲזִי דְּלָא מְצַוְוחַתְּ עֲלַהּ בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: and see that there is no outcry against it in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי קָקוּנָאֵי דְּאָתֵי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the rule of leaving out a section (שיור) when making an עירוב for a city
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city like קקונאי needs a carefully made עירוב, which רב יוסף assigns to אביי

steps.title: אביי chooses the river-facing houses as the left-out section
steps.stepSummary: אביי sees houses that open to the river and decides they will be the שיור, the section left out of the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and saw certain houses that opened to the river. He said: Let these be the left-out section for the city.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes his first decision. He picks the houses facing away from the city to be the required left-out section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the city may not be included in full, some part has to stay outside the עירוב. The houses opening to the river seemed like a convenient choice, because they don't open into the city anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The section of the city deliberately left out of the עירוב

phrases.english: He went and saw certain houses
that opened to the river.
He said: Let these be the left-out section for the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל, חֲזָא לְהָנְהוּ בָּתֵּי דִּפְתִיחִי לְנַהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי carries out רב יוסף's instruction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial plan: the houses opening to the river will serve as the שיור

steps.title: אביי retracts: the left-out section must be able to join
steps.stepSummary: אביי reconsiders. The משנה's wording "one may not include all of it" implies the left-out part must be something that could have been included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: We learned "one may not make an עירוב for all of it." This implies that if they wanted to make an עירוב, they would be able to.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects his own first plan, based on a careful reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids including "all of it," which assumes the whole city could have been included. So the left-out section must be a part that could have joined. The river houses don't open to the city, so they could never join. Leaving them out leaves out nothing real.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and said, meaning he retracted
They would be able to make an עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the river houses are outside the עירוב. The problem is that they could never have been inside it, so leaving them out does not count as a real שיור.

phrases.english: He then went back and said:
We learned: "One may not make an eiruv for all of it,"
which implies that if they wanted to make an eiruv,
they would be able to make an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan of step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's choice of the river-facing houses as the שיור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שיור must be an area that could have joined the עירוב. Houses with no opening to the city could never join.

steps.title: אביי makes windows so the houses can serve as the left-out section
steps.stepSummary: אביי fixes the problem by making windows from those houses to the city. Now they could join the עירוב, so they are a valid שיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, I will make windows for them, so that if they want to make an עירוב through the windows, they would be able to.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proposes a solution to the problem from step 12, which he will later reconsider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there are windows between those houses and the city, they could join the עירוב through the windows if they wanted to. That makes them a real section that could have been included, so leaving them out satisfies the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: At this stage אביי holds that a שיור must be an area that could have joined the עירוב, so he plans to open windows. This is only a temporary position. אביי retracts it in step 14, returns to it in step 15, and finally rejects it in step 16.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proposal sets up the back-and-forth that follows. The later steps test whether a שיור really must be a place that could have joined the עירוב. In the end, the proof from פומבדיתא in step 16 shows that it need not.

phrases.english: Rather, I will make windows for them,
so that if they want to make an eiruv
by way of the windows, they would be able to make an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem raised in step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By making windows, the river-facing houses become able to join the עירוב, so they can serve as the required שיור (a tentative view that אביי later drops)

steps.title: אביי retracts: windows are not needed, based on מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: אביי changes his mind. He says windows are unnecessary because רבה בר אבוה made separate עירובין for each neighborhood of מחוזא. Each neighborhood counted as the שיור for the others, even though they could never have joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: windows are not necessary. רבה בר אבוה made an עירוב for all of מחוזא neighborhood by neighborhood, because of the cattle-feeding ditches between them. Each neighborhood counted as the שיור for the others. This worked even though the neighborhoods could not have made one עירוב together if they had wanted to.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes back his decision to cut windows. He brings a real case showing that a שיור works even when it could never have joined the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, אביי said a שיור must be a place that could have been included. In מחוזא, ditches cut the neighborhoods off from each other, so they could not join. Yet each one still counted as the שיור for the others, so it seems the windows are not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said again (he changed his mind)
The section left out of the city's עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think מחוזא was left with no שיור. Every neighborhood had its own עירוב, and each neighborhood counted as the שיור for the others.

phrases.english: He then said again: it is not necessary,
phrases.notes: Not necessary to make the windows from step 13.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ מְעָרֵב לַהּ
phrases.english: for Rabba bar Avuh made an eruv for
all of Mechoza, neighborhood by neighborhood,
phrases.notes: Each neighborhood got its own separate עירוב.

phrases.english: because of the cattle-feeding ditches,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל חַד וְחַד הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר לְחַבְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: because each one counts as the left-out section for the other.
And even though, if they wanted

phrases.aramaic: לְעָרוֹבֵי בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי, לָא מָצוּ מְעָרְבִי.
phrases.english: to make an eruv together, they could not.
phrases.notes: This is the key point. The שיור could not have joined, yet it still worked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the conclusion of step 13 (making windows) by bringing a case that contradicts the reasoning of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need for windows and the requirement that a שיור be able to join the עירוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In practice, רבה בר אבוה used neighborhoods that could not join each other as one another's שיור.

steps.title: אביי retracts again: מחוזא is different, so windows are needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the comparison to מחוזא. There, the neighborhoods could have joined over the rooftops. The river houses have no way to join, so windows are needed after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: the cases are not the same. There, in מחוזא, if they wanted, they could have joined by way of the roofs. These houses cannot join at all. Therefore let us make windows.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against his own proof from step 14. He shows that מחוזא is not really a case of a שיור that could not join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ditches blocked the neighborhoods of מחוזא only at ground level. They could still have connected over the roofs, so they really were places that could have joined. The river houses have no such connection, so the rule from step 12 stands and windows are needed again.

phrases.english: He then said again: it is not comparable.
There, if they wanted,
they could join by way of the roofs,
but these houses cannot join,
phrases.notes: These means the houses facing the river in קקונאי.

phrases.english: therefore let us make windows for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from מחוזא in step 14 and goes back to the windows solution of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between מחוזא and the river houses.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The neighborhoods of מחוזא could have joined over the roofs, so they were not truly unable to join.

steps.title: אביי's final view: no windows needed, based on the straw storehouse
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that windows are not needed. In פומבדיתא, a straw storehouse belonging to מר בר פופידתא served as the city's שיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: windows are not needed either. That straw storehouse belonging to מר בר פופידתא of פומבדיתא was made the שיור for פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new proof showing that a שיור does not need to be a place that could have joined the עירוב. This is his final position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The straw storehouse of מר בר פופידתא could not have joined the city's עירוב. Yet it served as the שיור for all of פומבדיתא. This shows that a שיור does not have to be a place that could have joined, so the river houses work as a שיור without windows.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof from פומבדיתא settles אביי's question. A שיור does not need to be a place that could have joined the עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר: כַּוֵּוי נָמֵי לָא בָּעֵי,
phrases.english: He then said again: windows are also not necessary,
for that straw storehouse

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמָר בַּר פּוֹפִידְתָּא מִפּוּמְבְּדִיתָא,
phrases.english: that belonged to Mar bar Pofidata of Pumbedita,
they made it the left-out section for Pumbedita.
phrases.notes: A place that would not normally join the עירוב still served as the שיור.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: כַּוֵּוי נָמֵי לָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns step 15 again with a stronger proof that is not open to the roof argument.
steps.raayaObject: That a שיור does not need to be a place that could have joined the עירוב, so no windows are needed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice in פומבדיתא, where מר בר פופידתא's straw storehouse served as the city's שיור.

steps.title: אביי understands his teacher's warning
steps.stepSummary: אביי realizes this is what רב יוסף meant by telling him to make sure there would be no outcry in the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: this is what the Master told me: "See that there is no outcry about it in the study hall."
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. אביי realizes why רב יוסף warned him to make the עירוב beyond criticism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי went back and forth several times, and each time some new fact or precedent changed the answer. Now he sees how many things must be checked before deciding. That is why רב יוסף warned him that the work should leave no room for complaints in the study hall.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the Master told me
There is an outcry, a complaint

steps.whatToRemember: A city's עירוב needs a שיור, a section left out. אביי first thought the שיור must be a place that could have joined the עירוב. After going back and forth, he concluded from פומבדיתא that it does not need to be. The story also shows how carefully one must think before deciding a practical question.

phrases.english: He said: this is what the Master told me:
"See that there is no outcry about it in the study hall."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by connecting it back to רב יוסף's instruction in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Making a city's עירוב needs very careful thought. אביי's back-and-forth shows why רב יוסף demanded it be beyond criticism.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: leave out an area like the city of חדשה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה saying that a public city cannot be fully included in an עירוב unless an area the size of חדשה is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Unless he leaves outside of it an area like the city of חדשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can explain it. This is a setup for the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a city belonging to the public cannot be put entirely into one עירוב. Some section must stay out as a שיור. The measure it gives is 'like חדשה', but it does not say what that means, so the next step explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside of it, meaning left out of the עירוב
The city named חדשה in יהודה, used as the size measure

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חדשה' is the name of a real city. It does not mean a 'new city'.

phrases.english: Unless he made (left)
outside of it [an area] like the city of Ḥadasha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשָׂה חוּצָה לָהּ כָּעִיר חֲדָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of אביי and moves on to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public city may not be fully included in one עירוב unless an area like חדשה is left out.

steps.title: What the city of חדשה was
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: חדשה was a city in יהודה with fifty residents. The חכמים used it as the measure, and it was itself the שיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said, there was a city in יהודה named חדשה. It had fifty residents, counting men, women, and children. The חכמים used it as their measure, and it was itself the left-out section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain the משנה's phrase 'like חדשה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the size: a place with fifty residents. It also adds a new fact. חדשה was itself the left-out part for a larger city next to it, so the measure came from a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
They would measure (use as the size standard)
The left-out section that is not included in the עירוב

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was a certain city in Judea
and its name was Ḥadasha,
and it had fifty residents
men, women, and children,
and with it the Sages would measure,
and it was the excluded section.
phrases.notes: It was the left-out section for the large city next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the measure that the משנה mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The size of the שיור is like חדשה: fifty residents. חדשה was itself the שיור of a larger city.

steps.title: Did חדשה itself need a left-out section?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether חדשה could make its own עירוב for the whole town without leaving part of it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law for חדשה itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that the ברייתא did not answer. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חדשה served as the left-out part for the big city. But חדשה was also a city where many people lived. So does it need its own שיור when it makes an עירוב?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them: Ḥadasha, what is [the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's fact that חדשה was the שיור of another city.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חדשה needed its own שיור when it made an עירוב.

steps.title: Each city served as the other's left-out section
steps.stepSummary: Just as חדשה was the שיור for the big city, the big city was the שיור for חדשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חדשה: just as it was the left-out section for the big city, the big city was also the left-out section for the small one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חדשה did not need to leave out any of its own area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cities each made a separate עירוב. Each one was left out of the other's עירוב. So each city already had a שיור and was fully covered.

phrases.english: Ḥadasha, just as it
was the excluded section for the large [city] —
the large [city] also was the excluded section for the small one.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָשָׁה, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיהִי הָוְיָא שִׁיּוּר לִגְדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חדשה did not need its own שיור because the big city counted as its שיור.

steps.title: The real question: a small city that stands alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the question. What about a small city like חדשה that has no larger city next to it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is about a city like חדשה. What is its law?
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' tells us the גמרא is fixing its question. It now asks about a small city with no partner city. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חדשה itself had no problem because the big city covered it. The real doubt is about a small city that stands alone. Is a city that small already like a private area, so it needs no שיור?

phrases.english: Rather, [a city] like Ḥadasha, what is [the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the question after step 21 settled the case of חדשה itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a small city the size of חדשה, standing alone, needs a שיור.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says the small city needs a שיור. The other says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב יהודה disagreed. One said it needs a left-out section, and one said it does not need a left-out section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a disagreement and does not decide between the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view: any public city, even a small one, needs a שיור. The other view: a city as small as חדשה is already like a private area, so it needs none. The גמרא does not tell us who held which view.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which of the two (רב הונא or רב יהודה) held which opinion.

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda [disagreed]:
one said: it requires an excluded section,
and one said: it does not require an excluded section.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22, but only with a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: This is disputed. One אמורא requires a שיור and the other does not.
steps.whatToRemember: חדשה did not need its own שיור because the big city served as one. For a small city that stands alone, רב הונא and רב יהודה argue whether a שיור is needed.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה, who requires a שיור of three courtyards. רב rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: three courtyards, and so on. רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: the law follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next opinion in the משנה, then gives a ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds a smaller measure than רבי יהודה's fifty residents: three courtyards, each with two houses. רב rules that this is the law.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ חֲצֵירוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: three courtyards, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה: three courtyards of two houses each.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The law is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second opinion in the משנה about the size of the שיור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law follows רבי שמעון: a שיור of three courtyards is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for how much must be left out of an עירוב for a public city.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: even a much smaller area is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that even one house and one courtyard is enough as the שיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: even one house and one courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא offers an even smaller measure. The גמרא will question his wording in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק goes further than רבי שמעון's three courtyards. He holds that even a very small area left out is enough to serve as the שיור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
Even one house and one courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בַּיִת אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a smaller measure than רבי שמעון's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a very small area left out is enough as a שיור.

steps.title: Can a courtyard alone count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the wording. Could an empty courtyard with no house really count as the left-out section?
steps.simpleTranslation: One courtyard, can that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי יצחק's statement. This sets up the correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'a house and a courtyard' could be read as 'a house or even just a courtyard'. But a courtyard with no one living in it cannot work as a שיור, so the wording must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (meaning: surely not)

phrases.english: One courtyard, can it enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וְחָצֵר אַחַת' in רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An empty courtyard has no residents, so it cannot serve as a שיור.

steps.title: Corrected wording: one house in one courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording to 'one house in one courtyard'. A single lived-in house is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: one house in one courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by correcting the text of רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'and' to 'in' shows that he means a house standing in its courtyard. The minimum שיור is one lived-in house.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (a correction of the wording)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה requires a שיור like חדשה (fifty residents, per רבי יהודה) or three courtyards (רבי שמעון), and רב rules like רבי שמעון. רבי יצחק holds that even one house in one courtyard is enough.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
One house in one courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: בַּיִת אֶחָד בְּחָצֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק seemed to say that even an empty courtyard alone is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means one lived-in house standing in a courtyard.

steps.title: אביי asks about the source of רבי יצחק's ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether רבי יצחק's ruling (one house in one courtyard is enough) came from a tradition or from his own logic.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: This ruling of רבי יצחק, is it a tradition he received, or his own reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי wants to know where רבי יצחק's ruling from the previous steps comes from. Was it handed down from his teachers, or did he figure it out himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: גמרא here means a tradition passed down from teacher to student. סברא means a conclusion a scholar reached through his own logic. אביי is asking about the source of the ruling, not challenging the ruling itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A received tradition, learned from one's teachers
Logical reasoning; a scholar's own conclusion
An אמורא, student of רב יוסף

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does NOT mean 'the Talmud' or 'this page of גמרא.' It means 'a tradition received from one's teacher,' as opposed to סברא (one's own logic).

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
This ruling of Rabbi Yitzchak,
phrases.notes: That one house in one courtyard is enough as the שיור (Steps 25–27).

phrases.english: is it a received tradition, or his own reasoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the origin of the ruling that Step 27 just clarified.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי יצחק's ruling based on a received tradition or on his own logic?

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what difference it makes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף pushes back: either way the ruling is the same, so why does the source matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: What practical difference does it make to us?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף questions whether אביי's question is worth asking. The הלכה comes out the same either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge to the value of אביי's question. רב יוסף's point is that the practical law does not change, so knowing the source seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make to us?

phrases.english: He (Rav Yosef) said to him:
What difference does it make to us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question of Step 28 is worth asking.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's question about the source of רבי יצחק's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה is the same whether it is a tradition or logic, so the question seems to have no practical point.

steps.title: אביי explains that learning must be understood
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a saying: Is Torah learning just a song? We must understand what we learn, even with no practical difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: When you learn, is it just a song?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his question. Torah study is not like singing words you don't understand, so we try to understand every part of what the חכמים say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי turns down the idea that only practical differences are worth asking about. Knowing whether a ruling is a tradition or someone's own logic is part of truly understanding the Torah. This closes the discussion of רבי יצחק.
steps.whatToRemember: Torah learning is about understanding, not just knowing the bottom line. Asking 'where does this come from?' is worthwhile even when the הלכה doesn't change.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic גמרא statement about why we learn. Understanding is a goal in itself, beyond practical rulings.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
Learn your learning! Should it be just a song?!
phrases.notes: A well-known saying: learning without understanding is like singing lyrics you don't understand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise that only practical differences matter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A question with no practical difference is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Understanding the source and reasoning of the חכמים is valuable for its own sake.

steps.title: משנה: house within 2000, עירוב farther
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. A man is away from home when שבת starts, and his son put his עירוב on the opposite side. If his house is within 2000 אמות and the עירוב is farther, he may go to his house but not to the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone was in the east and told his son, 'Make an עירוב for me in the west.' Or he was in the west and told his son, 'Make an עירוב for me in the east.' If there are 2000 אמות from him to his house, and more than that to his עירוב, he may go to his house and may not go to his עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. A man is out on one side of town while his son sets his עירוב on the other side, so he cannot reach both his house and his עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Your שבת 'home base' must be within 2000 אמות of where you stand when שבת begins. Here only the house is within range, so the far-away עירוב does not work for him. He may walk to his house, and from there 2000 אמות in every direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Make an עירוב (food placed to set a שבת walking base) for me
2000 cubits: the תחום שבת, the walking limit on שבת
His עירוב: the spot where his food was placed to set his שבת home base

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'Make an עירוב for me' does not help if the man himself cannot reach that spot. What counts is the distance from where HE is standing when שבת starts.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who was in the east (of his home)
and said to his son: 'Make an eiruv for me in the west,'
(or he was) in the west and said to his son:
'Make an eiruv for me in the east,'

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ הֵימֶנּוּ וּלְבֵיתוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה,
phrases.english: if from him to his house there are 2000 amos,
and to his eiruv more than that,
he is permitted to go to his house, and forbidden to go to his eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the שיור discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the house is within 2000 אמות and the עירוב is beyond, he may go to his house, not to his עירוב.

steps.title: משנה: עירוב within 2000, house farther
steps.stepSummary: The reverse case: if the עירוב is within 2000 אמות and the house is farther, he may go to the עירוב but not to his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are 2000 אמות to his עירוב and more than that to his house, he may not go to his house, and he may go to his עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the mirror image of the last case. Now the עירוב is the spot within reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule applies in reverse. The עירוב is within 2000 אמות, so it takes effect and becomes his שבת home base. The house is now out of range for him.
steps.whatToRemember: Your שבת home base can only be a place within 2000 אמות of where you are when שבת starts. Whichever spot is in range wins.

phrases.english: (If) to his eiruv there are 2000 amos,
and to his house more than that,
he is forbidden to go to his house, and permitted to go to his eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעֵירוּבוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה, וּלְבֵיתוֹ יָתֵר מִכָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of Step 31's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the עירוב is within 2000 אמות and the house is beyond, he may go to the עירוב, not to his house.

steps.title: משנה: an עירוב in the city outskirts does nothing
steps.stepSummary: Placing an עירוב in the outskirts of the city (עיבורה של עיר) accomplishes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who places his עירוב in the outskirts of the city has not done anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule. An עירוב placed in the city's outskirts is useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outskirts (about 70 אמות around the city) already count as part of the city. A person's 2000 אמות are measured from the edge of the outskirts anyway, so placing an עירוב there gains him nothing extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The outskirts of the city (about 70⅔ אמות), counted as part of the city
He has done nothing at all

steps.confusionAlert: 'Did nothing' does not mean he is punished or loses his normal limit. He keeps the regular 2000 אמות from the city. The עירוב simply adds nothing.

phrases.english: One who places his eiruv
in the outskirts of the city,
has not done anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹתֵן אֶת עֵירוּבוֹ בְּעִיבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same משנה, about where an עירוב is placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב placed within the city's outskirts gives no extra walking range, since the outskirts already count as the city.

steps.title: Setting up the case of an עירוב placed just outside the city boundary
steps.stepSummary: The משנה introduces a new case: someone placed his עירוב outside the city's boundary, even by only one אמה. The ruling for this case comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he placed it outside the boundary, even one אמה beyond it...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up a new case that contrasts with Step 33: the עירוב is now placed past the city's edge instead of inside its outskirts. The ruling is not given here; the משנה is preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 33, an עירוב inside the city's outskirts did nothing, because the whole city already counts as one place. Here the עירוב is beyond that area, so it does take effect and creates a new home base. The words 'even one אמה' show that the smallest distance past the edge is enough to put the case into this new category, which sets up the result in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the boundary (here: past the edge of the city and its outskirts)
One cubit, a very small distance

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תחום' does not mean the 2000-אמה שבת limit. It means the edge of the city area that was discussed in Step 33. The עירוב is only slightly beyond the city, not 2000 אמות away.

phrases.english: If he placed it outside the boundary,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the עירוב. 'The boundary' means the edge of the city and its outskirts, which were discussed in Step 33.

phrases.english: even by just one cubit —
phrases.notes: The dash shows the sentence continues. The ruling comes on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None. This is a new clause of the משנה.
steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנוֹ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם, אֲפִילּוּ אַמָּה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 33. That step covered an עירוב inside the city's outskirts, which does nothing. This step opens the case of an עירוב placed just past that edge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling is not yet stated. This clause only defines the case: an עירוב placed even one אמה outside the city boundary. The result follows in the next part of the משנה.
